title: Bhuvneshwar Kumar Not Chasing India Recall as Ashwin Backs 2027 World Cup Return
excerpt: The veteran seamer says he has found peace away from the national team, even as calls grow for his inclusion in India's ODI World Cup squad.
body:
• Bhuvneshwar Kumar says he has made peace with life outside the Indian team and is no longer actively seeking a national recall.
  • R Ashwin has publicly backed the 36-year-old for India's 2027 ODI World Cup squad, saying "I think we would require him there."
  • Bhuvneshwar took 28 wickets in 16 matches in IPL 2026, helping RCB successfully defend their title as the tournament's second-highest wicket-taker.
  • India's pace bowling stocks beyond Bumrah and Siraj remain thin, with the World Cup in South Africa less than a year away.

Bhuvneshwar Kumar has broken his silence on the growing clamour for an India recall, striking a notably measured tone even as former teammate Ravichandran Ashwin campaigns for his inclusion in the 2027 ODI World Cup squad.

The 36-year-old seamer, whose stellar IPL 2026 campaign with Royal Challengers Bengaluru reignited the debate around his international future, made clear that another India cap is no longer the driving force behind his career. Speaking on the RCB Podcast, Bhuvneshwar credited his family for helping him find perspective after years away from the national setup.

"I am at peace, and I give credit to my family. At home, we never talk about cricket. We never talk about whether I'll get back into the Indian team, why I wasn't selected, or what went wrong."

— Bhuvneshwar Kumar, on the RCB Podcast

Ashwin Makes the Case

Bhuvneshwar's comments came days after Ashwin publicly pushed for his return, arguing that India's pace attack lacks the experience needed for a major ICC tournament. Speaking on a video shared through ESPNCricinfo's YouTube channel, the former off-spinner was unequivocal.

"Bhuvneshwar Kumar is a yes," Ashwin said. "I would tell him to do all the tournaments — first-class, the Vijay Hazare — everything. And get him ready for South Africa. I think we would require him there."

Ashwin drew a distinction between Bhuvneshwar and Mohammed Shami, who was part of India's Champions Trophy-winning squad in 2025. Bhuvneshwar's last ODI appearance came against South Africa in Paarl on January 21, 2022 — more than four years ago.

IPL Numbers That Demand Attention

The case for Bhuvneshwar rests heavily on his recent IPL form. In the 2026 season, he claimed 28 wickets from 16 matches for RCB, finishing as the tournament's second-highest wicket-taker. His consistency was central to Bengaluru's successful title defence, having also played a key role in their maiden IPL trophy the previous year. Across the last two seasons, Bhuvneshwar has taken 45 IPL wickets.

Despite those performances, the selectors have not included him in any of India's recent white-ball squads — not for the series against Afghanistan, Ireland, England, or Zimbabwe.

India's Pace Bowling Puzzle

The debate around Bhuvneshwar is inseparable from India's wider fast bowling concerns ahead of the 2027 ODI World Cup, to be co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia. Beyond Jasprit Bumrah and Mohammed Siraj, India's pace options lack international experience.

Bumrah remains injury-prone. He missed the deciding ODI against England at Lord's after sustaining a knee injury during the second match, a factor in India's series loss. The selectors have been rotating Gurnoor Brar, Prasidh Krishna, and Harshit Rana in the 50-over format, but none has established a firm grip on a World Cup spot.

Playing for the Love of It

Bhuvneshwar, who first made headlines by dismissing Sachin Tendulkar for a duck in a domestic first-class match early in his career, insists his motivations have shifted fundamentally. With 121 ODI caps and 141 wickets for India, including appearances at the 2015 and 2019 World Cups, he says he has nothing left to prove.

"I'm playing the IPL and domestic cricket because I love the game," he said. "I've already played for India. That's not something I have to achieve now. If I get another opportunity, that's great, but I've been there. Everything I'm doing now is because of my love for the game."

The right-arm seamer continues to feature in the UP T20 League and domestic tournaments, maintaining his fitness and match readiness while giving himself enough breaks to stay refreshed.

What's Next

With fewer than 12 months before the 2027 World Cup, time is running short for India to settle their pace bowling combination. The Vijay Hazare Trophy and domestic first-class season will offer both Bhuvneshwar and the selectors a window to assess whether his skills can translate back to international cricket after more than four years away.

Whether the selectors share Ashwin's conviction remains to be seen. Bhuvneshwar has made one thing clear: if the call comes, he will answer it — he just will not chase it.
